what_happened: An operator merged job pull request #149 by hand instead of using `athena land`. Two hand fixes had been added to the PR head beyond the job's landing commit, and the squash merge (02837e0, 2026-10-18) took them in with the job. Main's full history check then went red. The content was reverted and the commit was exempted. Two verified jobs were stranded by the revert.
cause: `athena land` judged the PR by the job's recorded landing commit, not by the PR's current head. It had no refusal for a head carrying extra commits. An operator who added fixes to the PR therefore had no supported way to land them, and merging by hand was the only route. Nothing else stopped a merge that skipped the history check, since the check ran only after the commit reached main.
prevention: Make `athena land` read the PR's current head. It should refuse, with a clear message, when the head holds any commit beyond the job's landing commit. It should also run the history check against that head before merging. Optionally add branch protection so merges can only go through land. Then a PR with extra fixes is stopped at land, and hand-merging has no reason to exist.
proposed_request: Change `athena land` so it judges the pull request's current head, not only the job's recorded landing commit. If the head holds any commit beyond the job's landing commit, land must refuse and say which extra commits it found and how to handle them (put the fix through its own job or a declared intervention). Before merging, land must run the full history check on the head and refuse if it fails. Show this with tests: a PR whose head has an extra hand-fix commit is refused, a clean PR lands, and a head that fails the history check is refused. Do not change how clean PRs land.
